subject: TermStack renewal: term extension, capacity uplift & MSA redlines
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@termstack.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@termstack.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal request — term extension + capacity uplift (TermStack / Redwood)

Hi David,

Thanks again for the productive call last week. TermStack is preparing our renewal request and we'd like to propose the following changes for the upcoming 12‑month term: 

- Term extension to 18 months (we need alignment on cancellation window)
- Capacity uplift: +40% baseline tokens/month, with a short burst pool for quarterly spikes
- A request for a one‑time onboarding credit to cover migration testing

I've attached a short PDF with our prioritized asks and a draft order form (TermStack_Renewal_Request.pdf). Legal asked us to surface any MSA changes up front — their counsel will push redlines if we make term/retention changes.

Can you confirm who on your side should own the contract redlines and what lead times you need for approvals? We're hoping to have paperwork routed by end of next week.

Appreciate it,
Elaine Park
Head of Cloud Ops, TermStack
elaine@termstack.com
+1 415‑555‑0192


From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@termstack.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal request — term extension + capacity uplift (TermStack / Redwood)

Thanks Elaine — got the PDF and the draft numbers. Looping in Ben (legal ops) and Lauren (rev ops) to scope the redline work and billing changes. Quick proposals from our side: 

- Legal: we can accept an 18‑month term but will need to clarify the early termination mechanics (pro rata vs. minimum commitment).
- Pricing: baseline increase is fine, but burst pools must be capped with an explicit per‑token surcharge; Lauren, can you provide cost delta and proration options?
- Credits: we can offer a one‑time migration credit (applied as a negative invoice line) — need procurement signoff.

Ben / Lauren — Elaine asked for a path to route MSA redlines and a sample order form with the new tiers. I'm attaching the MSA template with our usual comments (MSA_redlines_v1.docx). Please pull out the minimal set of legal changes we should accept to keep velocity high.

Timeline request from TermStack: paper sign by 2026‑06‑18. Is that feasible?

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine@termstack.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal request — term extension + capacity uplift (TermStack / Redwood)

David / Lauren / Elaine — reviewed the draft and summarized redline positions below. I've attached a tracked copy (redlines_MSA_v2.docx). High‑level: accept the term extension, propose the following guardrails to preserve our economics and liability posture.

1) Early termination: propose 60‑day cure notice and payment of pro rata fees for the remainder of the term, capped at 50% of remaining committed baseline for customer‑initiated terminations.
2) Data retention & deletion: if they request longer retention windows tied to the new term, we need explicit language on customer responsibility for retention costs and a KMS certification clause; otherwise, default to our standard 90‑day cache retention.
3) Burst pool: okay but require explicit ceiling (tokens/month) and 200% surcharge above baseline unit price for burst consumption; add automated soft‑alerts at 80% and hard caps configurable by account admin.
4) SLA credits: maintain current SLA language; do not expand credits for burst overage.

Open items for Lauren: billing proration approach (monthly vs. immediate invoice), how the migration credit shows on the invoice, and whether we can amortize credits across the first two invoices.

Elaine — can you confirm if TermStack needs the data retention change (Ben noted that is often the sticking point for legal)?

Ben Carter
LegalOps, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
--- Attachment: redlines_MSA_v2.docx (docx, 57KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine@termstack.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal request — term extension + capacity uplift (TermStack / Redwood)

David / Ben / Elaine — billing questions answered below: 

- Proration: we can offer either an immediate pro‑rata invoice at amendment (preferred) or spreading the delta across the remaining months of the current billing period. Immediate invoice shortens reconciliation but may be harder for their AR team.
- Migration credit: recommend a one‑time credit applied on the first post‑sign invoice. If TermStack prefers amortization, we can split across 2 invoices (max).
- DocuSign: I've prepared an order form with the new tiers; link below. Need TermStack billing contact for final review (procurement@termstack.com was CC'd).

Suggested next steps: 
1) Ben to finalize MSA redlines (accept the three guardrails above).
2) David to confirm pricing delta and select proration approach with Elaine.
3) We send DocuSign bundle (MSA + Order Form) for signature.

DocuSign (Order Form): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/TS-9812-sign

Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Elaine — thanks for the quick coordination this week. To confirm path forward based on Ben and Lauren's inputs: 

- Redwood accepts the 18‑month term with the early termination guardrails Ben proposed.
- We will cap burst pool consumption and apply the agreed surcharge; Lauren will include the exact rates on the order form.
- Migration credit: one‑time credit applied to first invoice (as Lauren suggested).
- Legal redlines: Ben will push the redline doc as final; we should be able to keep edits to a minimum so we can route to signature tomorrow.

If procurement is good with these points, we'll send the DocuSign bundle this afternoon. Elaine — please confirm the billing contact and we will route.

Thanks — David
